documents_checked.text:
The quality and extent of participation in learning and teaching activities may be a component
of assessment. Where participation is used for assessment, explicit marking criteria must be
identified and used, and a record must be kept by the Staff member conducting the class. The
participation component of a final grade will not normally exceed 10 percent of the total
marks.
While attendance at all scheduled learning activities is strongly encouraged and considered
essential for Student success, attendance may not be a component of grades for Students, i.e.
marks cannot be awarded for attendance alone. Attendance may be mandatory (required for
Unit completion) under certain circumstances. Reasons for mandatory attendance may
include:
statutory issues such as mandatory occupational health and safety training;
professional accreditation requirements; or
that a Student’s absence would have a significant effect on other Students’ studies.

documents_checked.text:
Authorised Users provided with accounts enabling access to University Information Systems
accept accounts on the understanding they are for the exclusive use of the Authorised User
and must not be shared or used by anyone other than the Authorised User.
Passwords, accounts and documented processes required for the access of University
information must be protected and secured in accordance with the conditions under which
access has been provided.
Authorised Users must not deliberately avoid or attempt to avoid authentication or conceal or
attempt to conceal their identity whilst using University information Systems.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Verification and admission of the disclosed proxy, and a valid basis for fulfilling any compulsory student participation.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Although N093 prohibits account sharing and N154 regulates mandatory attendance and participation, no relevant provision was identified in the documents and searches checked to verify or admit a disclosed AI proxy or establish whether it can validly fulfil compulsory participation.
case_summary.case_note: N154 regulates mandatory attendance and assessed participation while N093 restricts University ICT accounts to exclusive personal use, but neither policy addresses a disclosed AI avatar attending online classes. Consequently, ECU lacks any verification or admission pathway for a disclosed proxy and any basis for treating proxy attendance as valid compulsory participation. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review.

supporting_passages.text:
This policy applies to:
Complaints made by prospective, current and former Students or members of the public about
the University or University-related conduct, whether occurring in Australia or overseas; and
all persons involved in making, responding to, managing or resolving those Complaints.
Where legislation or another University or external framework provides a specific process for
dealing with all or part of a matter, the University may refer or manage that matter under the
applicable process. This includes matters concerning academic review or appeal, public
interest disclosures, misconduct, staff performance, privacy, employment or workplace
grievances, the ECU Student Guild, and third-party organisations.
This does not prevent the University from considering a distinct Complaint about its
administration of, or response to, the matter.
Where a matter engages more than one framework, the University will determine whether the
relevant issues are to be managed separately, sequentially, concurrently or in a coordinated
manner and will inform the Complainant of the applicable pathway.
